answer: Admission is an escalating auction, not a form. Each epoch releases a fixed batch of identity slots; the k-th slot costs k times the batch floor, so a farm buying n slots pays roughly n squared over two floors, and burned fees fund an umber pool that pays independent auditors. Slots and audit credit are non-transferable, and a slot whose first three attestations come from co-funded peers is voided before it may bid again. Bids stop at a summit price, above which slots are drawn by lottery among bidders, so a whale's win rate dilutes and every sold-out batch sends the floor into a spiral.
